housing.summary: Milan is Italy's most expensive rental market; central one-bedroom flats are in high demand and typically require a deposit plus first month upfront. Contracts are usually the 4+4 canone libero or 3+2 canone concordato type.

banking.summary: Opening a resident bank account requires an Italian tax code (codice fiscale) and proof of address; non-residents can open a conto non residente with a passport. Digital banks are widely used by newcomers before residency is finalised.

schools.summary: Milan has a broad range of international schools serving expatriate families, offering English-language and multilingual curricula alongside Italian state and private schools. Places at popular international schools should be secured well in advance.

legal_admin.summary: EU nationals staying over three months register residence with the local Comune (anagrafe); non-EU nationals must obtain a permesso di soggiorno after entry. Residence registration triggers issuance of a residence certificate and access to local services.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register residence (iscrizione anagrafica) at the Comune di Milano anagrafe office; non-EU arrivals first apply for a permesso di soggiorno at the Questura.

tax_finance.summary: Everyone needs a codice fiscale (Italian tax identification number) for employment, banking, renting and healthcare. It is issued by the Agenzia delle Entrate and required for almost all administrative processes.

transport.summary: Milan has an extensive integrated public transport network of metro, trams and buses operated by ATM, plus regional and suburban rail. Newcomers can exchange certain foreign driving licences and must register with the regional health service for medical care.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid and exchangeable; some non-EU licences may be exchanged under bilateral agreements, otherwise a new Italian licence is required.
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with the regional health service (Servizio Sanitario Regionale / ATS Milano) to obtain a tessera sanitaria and assigned general practitioner.
